candidates.mechanism: Nanoparticle-enhanced dielectric fluid improves breakdown voltage and partial discharge inception voltage through nanoparticle-base fluid interactions
candidates.intervention: Replace conventional transformer oil with nanofluid containing Al2O3 nanoparticles
candidates.expected_effect: Increased breakdown voltage and partial discharge inception voltage, reducing partial discharge activity
candidates.predicted_effect: Increased breakdown voltage and partial discharge inception voltage, reducing partial discharge activity
candidates.falsification_test: Transformer with 0.01% Al2O3 nanofluid will show 15% higher partial discharge inception voltage than conventional oil under identical test conditions

candidates.predicted_effect: Improved heat dissipation reducing hot spot temperatures
candidates.falsification_test: Transformer with 0.05% TiO2 nanofluid will show 10% reduction in top-oil temperature rise compared to conventional oil under identical load conditions

candidates.mechanism: Furanic compound generation from cellulosic paper degradation accelerates in aqueous environments
candidates.intervention: Implement furanic compound monitoring system with enhanced sensitivity to aqueous degradation products
candidates.expected_effect: Early detection of paper degradation through furanic compound concentration trends
candidates.predicted_effect: Early detection of paper degradation through furanic compound concentration trends
candidates.falsification_test: Transformers with developing paper insulation faults will show 2-FAL/5-HMF ratio increasing above 0.5 at least 30 days before conventional DGA detects fault gases

candidates.mechanism: Furanic compound distribution between oil and water phases varies by compound type
candidates.intervention: Implement dual-phase sampling system for oil and water compartments to track furanic compound distribution
candidates.expected_effect: Enhanced sensitivity to early-stage paper degradation through phase distribution analysis
candidates.predicted_effect: Enhanced sensitivity to early-stage paper degradation through phase distribution analysis
candidates.falsification_test: Transformers with developing insulation faults will show 30% higher furanic compound concentration in water phase compared to oil phase at least 30 days before conventional DGA detects fault gases

candidates.mechanism: Furanic compound derivatives transform into other compounds through degradation pathways
candidates.intervention: Implement derivative tracking system to monitor transformation of furanic compounds
candidates.expected_effect: Early warning of paper degradation through derivative transformation patterns
candidates.predicted_effect: Early warning of paper degradation through derivative transformation patterns
candidates.falsification_test: Transformers with developing insulation faults will show 5-MEF concentration increasing by 40% relative to 2-FAL at least 30 days before conventional DGA detects fault gases

candidates.mechanism: Thermal degradation of cellulose insulation accelerates exponentially with temperature, following the Arrhenius law, leading to reduced mechanical strength and increased gas generation
candidates.intervention: Implement a thermal model that uses top-oil temperature, load current, and ambient temperature to estimate the hottest-spot temperature and calculate the cumulative thermal aging of the insulation
candidates.expected_effect: A measurable increase in the rate of insulation degradation as calculated by the model will correlate with increased gas generation rates detectable before conventional DGA
candidates.predicted_effect: A measurable increase in the rate of insulation degradation as calculated by the model will correlate with increased gas generation rates detectable before conventional DGA
candidates.falsification_test: When the calculated thermal aging rate exceeds 0.5% per day, gas generation rates will increase by at least 20% compared to the previous 30-day average

candidates.mechanism: Partial discharge activity in insulation voids produces gases and creates conductive carbonized tracks, leading to progressive insulation breakdown
candidates.intervention: Install acoustic emission sensors to detect partial discharge activity and correlate with electrical and thermal parameters to identify discharge patterns characteristic of developing faults
candidates.falsification_test: When acoustic emissions exceed background noise by 15dB for more than 2 hours, partial discharge activity will be confirmed within 7 days and gas generation rates will increase within 30 days

candidates.mechanism: Oil decomposition under thermal stress produces hydrogen and methane gases, with gas ratios indicating specific fault types according to the Duval triangle
candidates.intervention: Implement a gas generation rate model using tank pressure trends, temperature history, and load profiles to predict gas generation rates before they accumulate to detectable levels
candidates.expected_effect: A sudden increase in the calculated gas generation rate will precede abnormal gas ratios in DGA samples by at least 30 days
candidates.predicted_effect: A sudden increase in the calculated gas generation rate will precede abnormal gas ratios in DGA samples by at least 30 days
candidates.falsification_test: When the calculated gas generation rate exceeds 2.5% of the total dissolved gas capacity per week, abnormal gas ratios will be detected in the next DGA sample
